rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants who report violations or organize
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, or joining a tenants' union. The landlord is liable for 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater) plus attorney's fees. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change in terms within six months of protected activity is presumed to be a reprisal. Lease waivers are void.
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.
rules.key_value: Damages of 1-3 months' rent or actual damages; 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal
rules.penalty: Damages not less than one month's rent or more than three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state an effective date.

parsed.doc_summary: G.L. c. 186, § 18 (Massachusetts) bars landlord reprisals against tenants who report violations, enforce housing laws, or organize. It sets damages of 1 to 3 months' rent and a 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal after protected activity. One record is extracted under just_cause_eviction.
